Every pattern P1-P15 gained a one-line **Targeted reads:** field (P5/P6 exception handlers, P8 writes to the process environment, P10 the loop around a bulk or full pull, etc.). P6 and P10 say to raise to med when the fallback or the full pull sits in the request path. P8's look-for covers request code copying a user's credentials into the process environment. New P16 'Readiness with no loading state or retry in the client' (anchor node, design, med) has the client's health/readiness call as its targeted read. scripts/pipeline.mjs: new exported catalogueReads(text) parses the patterns and their Targeted reads lines. reviewerBrief() adds a '## Targeted reads' section listing '- <pattern heading>: <reads>' for every pattern, read from the catalogue at render time so the catalogue stays the single source. The budget line is now 'the targeted reads below, then at most 12 more reads, only to confirm'. The brief came to ~4.3K characters, over the shared 4000 BRIEF_CAP, so writeBrief takes a cap argument and the reviewer brief uses a new exported REVIEWER_BRIEF_CAP = 8000 (room for two 200-character work paths and an update's touched ids). Explorer and synthesizer briefs keep BRIEF_CAP. agents/archmap-reviewer.md: the input rule and the 'How to work' list (now 6 steps) say to make the brief's targeted reads and name the four code-only patterns. The calibrated wording and the three-line reply are unchanged. Adjacent file outside the task's files: skills/architecture-map/SKILL.md line 356 still said the reviewer gets 'at most 12 targeted reads only to confirm a specific claim'. I edited it to match the new behaviour (targeted reads, then at most 12 confirming reads), and the plan gate (hooks/require-plan.py) allowed the edit. Not done: the description's optional item, letting prescan or the explorer brief carry cheap facts. That would touch prescan/extract files outside this task's scope and is left for a follow-up.
